mechanism_narrative: A sustained low level of federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which may lead to increased borrowing and investment, thus driving up the S&P 500 over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the periods following low FEDFUNDS, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate below 3.5% signals a strong labor market, which may lead to increased consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 does not show positive returns in more than 60% of the periods when UNRATE is below 3.5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Positive growth in both GDP and housing starts indicates a strong demand environment, which may boost corporate revenues and drive up the S&P 500 over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 50% of the periods following positive GDP and housing starts growth, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production, especially during an economic expansion, may lead to increased efficiency and output, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 does not show positive returns in more than 50% of the periods when industrial production increases during expansion, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Growth in non-farm payroll employment indicates a strong labor market, which may lead to increased economic activity and higher S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the periods following payroll growth, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in real consumer spending may indicate strong demand, leading to higher corporate revenues and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 does not show positive returns in more than 60% of the periods when RSAFS increases by more than 0.5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in federal funds rate alongside a decrease in unemployment rate may signal a tightening monetary policy, which could lead to decreased borrowing and investment, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 40% of the periods when FEDFUNDS rises and UNRATE falls, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rising federal funds rate during a monetary tightening cycle may lead to increased borrowing costs and reduced investment, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 50% of the periods when FEDFUNDS is above 2%, the hypothesis is rejected.
